h1: What needs approval in a Newton local historic district?
title: Newton Local Historic Districts: What Needs Review
description: In a Newton local historic district, exterior changes, including hardscaping, need Historic District Commission review. How the certificates work.
short_answer: In a Newton local historic district, exterior changes, including hardscaping, need review by the Historic District Commission. Visible alterations need a Certificate of Appropriateness. In-kind work, changes that can't be seen, and excluded work can get a Certificate of Non-Applicability, and in-kind repairs may qualify for administrative approval.

facts.text: Exterior changes in a local historic district, including hardscaping, require HDC review.
A Certificate of Appropriateness covers visible alterations the commission finds appropriate.
A Certificate of Non-Applicability covers in-kind work, changes that can't be seen, or excluded work.
Exterior building changes require an application, and in-kind repairs may qualify for administrative approval.

qa.q: Do I need approval to replace windows in a historic district?
qa.a: Exterior building changes need an application. In-kind work may qualify for a Certificate of Non-Applicability or administrative approval.

qa.q: Does a patio or walkway need review?
qa.a: The City says exterior changes, including hardscaping, need HDC review.

qa.q: What is a Certificate of Appropriateness?
qa.a: Approval for visible alterations that the commission finds appropriate.

items: Whether your property is inside a local historic district.
